Building on [Animation Loop](../webgpu-animation-loop/), the particles now move. Each
one has a velocity, and every step its position is advanced and reflected off the
walls. The new idea is the _fixed timestep_: physics advances in constant steps of
1/120 s, however fast the browser redraws, so the simulation behaves the same on
every display. There is almost no new WebGPU here; positions are simply rewritten
into the storage buffer each frame with `writeBuffer`.

```{ojs}
//| column: page
//| code-fold: true
//| code-summary: "Show code"
{
  // Shared WebGPU boilerplate: setup, buffers and the animation loop (lib/gpu.js)
  const gpu = await import(new URL("../lib/gpu.js", document.baseURI).href);

  // Setup, as before (640x480 buffer, scaled to fill the column)
  const { canvas, device, context, format } = await gpu.setup();

  // Simulation state lives on the CPU, in clip space (-1 to 1)
  const count = 50;
  const half = [0.03 * 0.75, 0.03]; // particle half-size; x scaled by 4:3 aspect
  const positions = new Float32Array(count * 2);
  const velocities = new Float32Array(count * 2);
  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    positions[2 * i] = (Math.random() * 2 - 1) * (1 - half[0]);
    positions[2 * i + 1] = (Math.random() * 2 - 1) * (1 - half[1]);
    const angle = Math.random() * 2 * Math.PI;
    const speed = 0.3 + Math.random() * 0.5; // clip units per second
    velocities[2 * i] = Math.cos(angle) * speed;
    velocities[2 * i + 1] = Math.sin(angle) * speed;
  }

  // Advance the simulation by one fixed step of `dt` seconds
  function step(dt) {
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      for (let axis = 0; axis < 2; axis++) {
        const k = 2 * i + axis;
        const limit = 1 - half[axis];
        positions[k] += velocities[k] * dt;
        // Bounce: clamp to the wall and flip the velocity
        if (positions[k] > limit) {
          positions[k] = limit;
          velocities[k] = -velocities[k];
        } else if (positions[k] < -limit) {
          positions[k] = -limit;
          velocities[k] = -velocities[k];
        }
      }
    }
  }

  // Storage buffer: the positions, rewritten every frame
  const positionBuffer = device.createBuffer({
    size: positions.byteLength,
    usage: GPUBufferUsage.STORAGE | GPUBufferUsage.COPY_DST,
  });

  // Vertex buffer: one unit square (two triangles), shared by every particle
  const cornerBuffer = gpu.unitSquare(device);

  // Shaders
  const module = device.createShaderModule({
    code: `
      @group(0) @binding(0) var<storage, read> positions: array<vec2f>;

      @vertex
      fn vs(
        @location(0) corner: vec2f,
        @builtin(instance_index) i: u32,
      ) -> @builtin(position) vec4f {
        let half = vec2f(${half[0]}, ${half[1]});
        return vec4f(positions[i] + corner * half, 0.0, 1.0);
      }

      @fragment
      fn fs() -> @location(0) vec4f {
        return vec4f(1.0, 0.282, 0.204, 1.0); // #FF4834
      }
    `,
  });

  // Pipeline
  const pipeline = device.createRenderPipeline({
    layout: "auto",
    vertex: {
      module,
      entryPoint: "vs",
      buffers: [gpu.squareLayout],
    },
    fragment: {
      module,
      entryPoint: "fs",
      targets: [{ format }],
    },
    primitive: { topology: "triangle-list" },
  });

  // Bind group: plug the positions into the shader
  const bindGroup = device.createBindGroup({
    layout: pipeline.getBindGroupLayout(0),
    entries: [{ binding: 0, resource: { buffer: positionBuffer } }],
  });

  // One frame: upload the current positions, then record and submit a render pass
  function draw() {
    device.queue.writeBuffer(positionBuffer, 0, positions);

    const encoder = device.createCommandEncoder();
    const pass = gpu.beginRenderPass(encoder, context);
    pass.setPipeline(pipeline);
    pass.setBindGroup(0, bindGroup);
    pass.setVertexBuffer(0, cornerBuffer);
    pass.draw(6, count); // 6 vertices per square, `count` instances
    pass.end();
    device.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
  }

  // Fixed-timestep loop. Real elapsed time goes into an accumulator, and
  // physics drains it in constant steps of `dt`. Rendering happens once per
  // browser frame, whatever the refresh rate.
  const dt = 1 / 120;
  let accumulator = 0;
  let last = null;

  function frame(ms) {
    const now = ms / 1000;
    // Clamp the elapsed time so a backgrounded tab doesn't trigger a huge catch-up
    const elapsed = last === null ? 0 : Math.min(now - last, 0.25);
    last = now;
    accumulator += elapsed;
    while (accumulator >= dt) {
      step(dt);
      accumulator -= dt;
    }
    draw();
  }
  gpu.run(invalidation, device, frame);

  yield canvas;
}
```
